_doc: Registered camera poses for gate Q16 (schema 2). Nothing here is a measured 1863 camera position. Per pose: statement_ids point into position_statements.json (what the sources literally say); position.tier is inferred (a statement plus mapped objects fix it to about the sigma_m given) or plausible-procedural (an assumption); there is no documented-position tier in use because no source gives a coordinate, a lens and a plate (decision DD-PM-01). position.place_documented = true (poses P27, P28, P29, third pass) marks a camera place that a source other than a lead names as a building of known outline, with a cardinal word for the direction (decision DD-PM-06): the position is still inferred, its sigma is the outline, the camera height is an assumption. fitted_to_photograph = a number (the distance) was taken from the photograph itself, so a match there is not an independent test. superseded_by / supersedes link a pose to the better-sourced pose that replaced it for the same record (its verdict is kept); also_loc_ids lists other prints of the same exposure. The DEM is modern bare ground (no 1863 trees, rocks, crops); heights are the model's, 1.6 m above ground unless agl_m says otherwise. A person's verdict per pose is in verdicts.json.

position.basis: The NPS places the camera on the summit / crest of Little Round Top (Little Round Top CLR Fig. 4.05; Common Pride vol. 3 p. 452; Then-And-Now). The summit is a rock outcrop about 100 m long; the statue of Warren (monument list no. 101, on the summit boulder) stands on it. Coordinates = highest DEM cell within 25 m of the statue; the exact tripod spot on the outcrop is not published.

heading.basis: NPS: looking northward; Ziegler's Grove dominates the horizon at the left centre (Common Pride p. 452). Heading = bearing to the gazetteer centre of Ziegler's Grove plus 4 degrees (one tenth of the assumed 40-degree field) so that the grove falls left of centre; the gazetteer centre carries sigma 221 m.

poses.note: The NPS names Codori Grove, the Copse of Trees, the tree at the head of Brien Lane, Ziegler's Grove, Cemetery Hill and Patterson on its annotated plate (Common Pride vol. 3, printed p. 453, read from the page image); the model stand-ins are the Codori house, the High Water Mark monument (the Copse), the Ziegler's Grove gazetteer centre, the Cemetery Hill gazetteer centre and the Patterson farmstead symbols.

position.basis: NPS: the exposure with the negative number LC-B815-273 looks north from the roof of the Evergreen Cemetery lodge (Cultural Landscape Report for Gettysburg National Cemetery, Fig. 1.26, printed p. 23, pdf page marker 42); the LOC record 2018671576 carries that call number (statement PS-NPS-CLRCEM-126). The coordinates are the centroid of the 2023 outline of the gatehouse (STR-TOWN-GATEHOUSE, err 4 m; the outline includes the right-hand addition, the 1863 form may have been smaller), so the horizontal position is known to about the size of the building (sigma 20 m); no source gives the roof height or the spot on the roof. Feature matching (SIFT, RANSAC homography, 2026-11-14) of the print against the two frames of the stereo negative: 204 and 170 inliers, median residual 1.0 px, no growth of the residual from the far town (rows 0.4 to 0.6) to the near road (rows 0.8 to 1.0: 1.7 and 1.3 px): one homography explains every depth, so the prints and the frames show the same view from the same station to within the pixel noise (the shared negative or a stereo camera beside the large one); no source states it.

poses.agl_basis: ASSUMPTION: camera on the roof of a two-storey brick building: 8 m above the DEM ground (eaves about 7 to 8 m); no source gives it; the effect on the far field is below one degree, on the road and the walls 10 to 30 m away it is large

heading.basis: NPS (Cultural Landscape Report for Gettysburg National Cemetery, Fig. 1.26): 'looking north'; north = 0 degrees, a cardinal word (about 22 degrees either way); not adjusted to the photograph. Two other NPS texts (Record of Treatment, volumes I and II) call the same exposure, as LOC ppmsca 35051, a view northwest (scenario carried as pose P28); the Baltimore Pike runs from the lodge toward bearing 326 degrees and the borough lies at about 352 degrees.
